summary: Built the pure intel rules. packages/simulation/src/intel has the config, a 3x3 sectorOf, a world view that does not import the ledger, stepIntel(config,state,view,requests)->{state,messages,outcomes} and targetedRumorAvailability. They cover start/fresh/targeted/replacement rumors (sources, then caches, then carrier sighting), journal staleness and resolution, two-snapshot carrier sightings (30-60 s old), the per-snapshot sighting cap with deferred free triggers, request-id outcomes including duplicate, the first-full-set sector and route (lost, restored, second completer), and the minute-20 and minute-28/30 s reveals, all fired on crossed boundaries. packages/content/src/intel has the constants and a zod validator. Both packages got an ./intel subpath export, and docs/intel.md is written. Tests: sectors.test.ts (7), intel.test.ts (19 scripted), property.test.ts (7 seeded runs, including a real-constant slice run of 36,660 ticks and skip-tick runs, with hidden-information checks, replay hash and EXERCISED), and a content test (3). Checks run in this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (569/569 pass), npm run test:integration (36/36 pass), npm run build (exit 0). I also injected bugs one at a time (newest snapshot, no cap, own copies, never stale, route without set, pending never delivered, leaked id); the tests failed for each, and the source was restored afterwards.
open_assumptions: Held types and claimed-out islands are derived from the view's rubbings (carried + duel-reserved; islands with no sealed source), rather than passed as separate fields that could disagree.
Pending deferred sightings are kept at most one per type, not one per player, so that 'deferred, never dropped' holds when two types need a sighting at once. They are delivered one per snapshot.
A free trigger with every copy carried but no usable older-snapshot entry (for example before the second snapshot) is deferred like a capped one. A targeted request in that case gets 'none'.
sightingDelayTicks must equal carrierIntervalTicks (the validator enforces this), because sightings read the previous snapshot.
Targeted requests are answered 'none' before control start or for an unknown player. A targeted rumor never repeats a target already active in the player's journal.
Targeted requests in one batch are processed in request-id order. Outcomes are returned in the order given.
untested: scripts/smoke-build.ts lists workspace exports explicitly and is outside the owned paths, so npm run build does not load @pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel or @pirate-sea-race/content/intel from dist. I checked this by hand with a node import after the build.
Integration with the real ledger and MatchRoom (world view construction) is not exercised; that is objectives-endgame's job.
Property runs use a test-local world simulator, not the ledger's operations.
verify_yourself: That allowing up to one pending sighting per type (rather than strictly one per player) is an acceptable reading of 'at most one pending per player' given the 'deferred, never dropped' rule.
